claim: Let \(m\ge2\), let \(p_1,\ldots,p_m>0\) with \(\sum_i p_i=1\), and let \(U_1,\ldots,U_m\in U(4)\) act on \(\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^2\). Put \(\mathcal E(\rho)=\sum_i p_iU_i\rho U_i^\dagger\) and \(V_m=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{U_i^\dagger U_j:1\le i,j\le m\}\). For Haar-almost every ordered \(m\)-tuple, if \(m\in\{2,3,4\}\) then \(\dim V_m=m^2-m+1\) and \(V_m\cap(M_2\otimes I_2)=V_m\cap(I_2\otimes M_2)=\mathbb C I_4\). Hence neither party has a nontrivial first local measurement in Cohen's channel-LOCC criterion, and the channel is not LOCC even with infinitely many rounds. For every \(m\ge5\), Haar-almost surely \(V_m=M_4(\mathbb C)\); both local intersections are the full four-dimensional local matrix algebras, and each party admits a nontrivial positive two-outcome first local measurement, so this first-round obstruction vanishes. Thus five random unitaries are the exact generic threshold for disappearance of the first-round obstruction in the two-qubit case. No claim is made that the \(m\ge5\) channels are LOCC.

integrity.computational_dependence: The theorem is analytic; the exact modular checker certifies one nonvanishing witness used in the genericity proof.
integrity.novelty_scope: Exact Haar-generic two-qubit threshold for Cohen first-round obstruction: non-LOCC for two through four random unitaries, obstruction vanishing from five onward.
integrity.prior_work_preserved: Cohen is credited with the channel criterion and the numerical random-unitary transition evidence.

scientific_limitations: The theorem is for two-qubit random-unitary channels and Haar-almost-every unitary tuple.
For five or more unitaries the theorem proves only disappearance of the first-round linear LOCC obstruction, not LOCC implementability.
Exceptional structured unitary tuples are not classified.
A differently phrased later proof could exist outside the searched literature.
title: A sharp generic five-unitary first-round threshold for two-qubit random-unitary channels
